senselab.utils.work_pool

A work queue on shared storage: items, leases, heartbeats and re-publishing, with a worker that runs them.

A pool is a directory that every node can see::

pool.json                    the pool's settings (schema ``work-pool-1``)
queue/<item>.json            published, unclaimed items
leases/<item>/               a claimed item: item.json, owner.json, heartbeat, attempt
tmp/                         claim, publish and hand-off staging
interrupted/<item>.<a>.json  attempt ``a`` was released or reaped
done/<item>.json             the item succeeded (exit code, host, times)
failed/<item>.<a>.json       attempt ``a`` failed
dead/<item>.json             the item spent its failure or interruption budget
conflicts/<item>.<why>.<t>.json  a duplicate copy of an item, kept out of the queue
workers/<worker>.json        the workers that ran here
hostcheck/<p>.<worker>.<t>.json  a worker on partition ``p`` failed its host check (before claiming anything)
controller/                  the controller's lock, the jobs it submitted (jobs/<id>.json), stale markers
status.json                  written by `WorkPool.status()` (and `Controller`, with ``partitions``)

An item is always in one place. WorkPool.claim() takes it with rename(queue/<i>.json, tmp/claim-<token>/item.json) into a dir that already holds owner.json and a heartbeat, and publishes the lease with rename(tmp/claim-<token>, leases/<i>). WorkPool.complete(), WorkPool.fail(), WorkPool.release() and WorkPool.reap() all start by renaming leases/<i> aside, so only one of them acts on a lease; the next state is written as a new file there and placed with an exclusive link(2) (done/, dead/, or queue/ with attempt+1). After a rename or link reports an error, the destination is read back for the caller's token, because a retransmitted NFS call can report failure to the process that made it. Ages are measured on the storage's clock.

python -m senselab.utils.work_pool work POOL --classes a,b runs a worker: claim, run the item's command with POOL_ITEM_ID and POOL_ATTEMPT set, heartbeat, then complete or fail; SIGTERM releases the item.

python -m senselab.utils.work_pool control POOL --classes classes.yaml runs a Controller: each tick reaps, counts queued items per class and this pool's Slurm workers per partition, and submits or cancels workers.

Ported and generalised from sensein/senselab@feat/task-events (f2a806af), specs/20261011-slice-pool/pool/slice_pool.py. Standard library only.

   1"""A work queue on shared storage: items, leases, heartbeats and re-publishing, with a worker that runs them.
   2
   3A pool is a directory that every node can see::
   4
   5    pool.json                    the pool's settings (schema ``work-pool-1``)
   6    queue/<item>.json            published, unclaimed items
   7    leases/<item>/               a claimed item: item.json, owner.json, heartbeat, attempt
   8    tmp/                         claim, publish and hand-off staging
   9    interrupted/<item>.<a>.json  attempt ``a`` was released or reaped
  10    done/<item>.json             the item succeeded (exit code, host, times)
  11    failed/<item>.<a>.json       attempt ``a`` failed
  12    dead/<item>.json             the item spent its failure or interruption budget
  13    conflicts/<item>.<why>.<t>.json  a duplicate copy of an item, kept out of the queue
  14    workers/<worker>.json        the workers that ran here
  15    hostcheck/<p>.<worker>.<t>.json  a worker on partition ``p`` failed its host check (before claiming anything)
  16    controller/                  the controller's lock, the jobs it submitted (jobs/<id>.json), stale markers
  17    status.json                  written by :meth:`WorkPool.status` (and :class:`Controller`, with ``partitions``)
  18
  19An item is always in one place. :meth:`WorkPool.claim` takes it with ``rename(queue/<i>.json,
  20tmp/claim-<token>/item.json)`` into a dir that already holds ``owner.json`` and a heartbeat, and publishes the
  21lease with ``rename(tmp/claim-<token>, leases/<i>)``. :meth:`WorkPool.complete`, :meth:`WorkPool.fail`,
  22:meth:`WorkPool.release` and :meth:`WorkPool.reap` all start by renaming ``leases/<i>`` aside, so only one of
  23them acts on a lease; the next state is written as a new file there and placed with an exclusive ``link(2)``
  24(``done/``, ``dead/``, or ``queue/`` with attempt+1). After a rename or link reports an error, the destination is
  25read back for the caller's token, because a retransmitted NFS call can report failure to the process that made
  26it. Ages are measured on the storage's clock.
  27
  28``python -m senselab.utils.work_pool work POOL --classes a,b`` runs a worker: claim, run the item's command with
  29``POOL_ITEM_ID`` and ``POOL_ATTEMPT`` set, heartbeat, then complete or fail; SIGTERM releases the item.
  30
  31``python -m senselab.utils.work_pool control POOL --classes classes.yaml`` runs a :class:`Controller`: each tick
  32reaps, counts queued items per class and this pool's Slurm workers per partition, and submits or cancels workers.
  33
  34Ported and generalised from ``sensein/senselab@feat/task-events`` (f2a806af),
  35``specs/20261011-slice-pool/pool/slice_pool.py``. Standard library only.

  61SCHEMA = "work-pool-1"
  62"""The ``schema`` value of ``pool.json``."""
  63
  64SUBDIRS = (
  65    "queue",
  66    "leases",
  67    "tmp",
  68    "interrupted",
  69    "done",
  70    "failed",
  71    "dead",
  72    "conflicts",
  73    "workers",
  74    "hostcheck",

  77"""The pool's subdirectories."""

  79ID_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,199}")
  80"""What an item id may look like (it names files)."""
  81
  82DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 2
  83"""Failed attempts an item may have before it goes to ``dead/``."""
  84
  85DEFAULT_MAX_INTERRUPTS = 6
  86"""Releases and reaps an item may have before it goes to ``dead/`` (reason ``interrupts``)."""
  87
  88KILL_GRACE_S = 10.0
  89"""Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL when a worker stops its child's process group."""
  90
  91SIGNAL_GRACE_S = 3.0
  92"""Seconds a worker waits for its own SIGTERM handler after its child died of a signal."""
  93
  94SIGNAL_EXIT = 143
  95"""A worker's exit code after SIGTERM."""
  96
  97PUTBACK_WAIT_S = 1.0
  98"""Seconds before a lease found absent is checked again: a reaper that renamed a live lease aside puts it back."""
  99
 100JOIN_GRACE_S = 5.0
 101"""Extra seconds a worker waits for its heartbeat thread to stop after a run."""
 102
 103MOVED = ".moved-"
 104"""Prefix of a marker file created in a dir just renamed into ``tmp/``, so the dir's mtime (its age) counts from
 105the move. Ages are read from the dir alone: an open of a file inside would make the NFS client keep a
 106``.nfs*`` copy of it when its owner deletes it, and the owner's removal of the dir would fail."""
 107
 108REMOVE_RETRY_S = 1.0
 109"""Seconds a dir removal keeps retrying while an NFS ``.nfs*`` placeholder (a file open elsewhere) blocks it."""
 110
 111NEXT = "next.json"
 112"""The next state of an item in a hand-off dir, placed with ``link(2)``."""
 113
 114HOST_CHECK_EXIT = 3
 115"""A worker's exit code after its host check failed (it claimed nothing)."""
 116
 117HOST_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S = 300.0
 118"""Seconds a host check may run before it counts as failed."""
 119
 120CONTROLLER_LOCKED_EXIT = 4
 121"""A controller's exit code when another controller holds the pool's lock."""

 123PathLike = Union[str, Path]
 124
 125
 126def _now() -> float:
 127    return time.time()
 128
 129
 130def _host() -> str:
 131    return socket.gethostname().split(".")[0]
 132
 133
 134GONE_ERRNOS = (errno.ENOENT, errno.ENOTDIR, errno.ESTALE)
 135"""Errors that mean a path is gone; NFS reports ESTALE for a path another node renamed away mid-lookup."""
 136
 137
 138def _gone(exc: OSError) -> bool:
 139    return exc.errno in GONE_ERRNOS
 140
 141
 142def _names(path: Path) -> list[str]:
 143    """Directory entries, without dot-files (in-progress writes)."""
 144    try:
 145        return [name for name in os.listdir(path) if not name.startswith(".")]
 146    except OSError as exc:
 147        if _gone(exc):
 148            return []
 149        raise
 150
 151
 152def _write_json(path: Path, data: Any) -> None:  # noqa: ANN401
 153    """Write JSON through a temporary file beside it and an atomic rename."""
 154    tmp = path.with_name(f".{path.name}.{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}.tmp")
 155    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
 156    os.replace(tmp, path)
 157
 158
 159def _read_json(path: Path) -> Any:  # noqa: ANN401
 160    """The file's JSON; None when it is absent or unreadable as JSON."""
 161    try:
 162        with open(path) as handle:
 163            return json.load(handle)
 164    except json.JSONDecodeError:
 165        return None
 166    except OSError as exc:
 167        if _gone(exc):
 168            return None
 169        raise
 170
 171
 172def _exists(path: Path) -> bool:
 173    """Whether a path exists, asked through an open (revalidated with an NFS server) rather than a cached stat."""
 174    try:
 175        os.close(os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY))
 176    except OSError as exc:
 177        if _gone(exc):
 178            return False
 179        raise
 180    return True
 181
 182
 183def _fresh_mtime(path: Path) -> Optional[float]:
 184    """The file's mtime through an open; None when it is absent."""
 185    try:
 186        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
 187        try:
 188            return os.fstat(fd).st_mtime
 189        finally:
 190            os.close(fd)
 191    except OSError as exc:
 192        if _gone(exc):
 193            return None
 194        raise
 195
 196
 197def _fresh_times(path: Path) -> Optional[float]:
 198    """The later of the path's mtime and ctime through an open; None when it is absent."""
 199    try:
 200        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
 201        try:
 202            st = os.fstat(fd)
 203            return max(st.st_mtime, st.st_ctime)
 204        finally:
 205            os.close(fd)
 206    except OSError as exc:
 207        if _gone(exc):
 208            return None
 209        raise
 210
 211
 212def _mark_moved(directory: Path) -> None:
 213    """Create a fresh marker file in a dir, which sets the dir's mtime on the storage's clock."""
 214    try:
 215        os.close(os.open(directory / f"{MOVED}{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}", os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o660))
 216    except OSError as exc:
 217        if not _gone(exc):
 218            raise
 219
 220
 221def _remove_dir(path: Path) -> None:
 222    """Remove a dir tree, retrying briefly while an NFS ``.nfs*`` placeholder blocks it."""
 223    deadline = time.monotonic() + REMOVE_RETRY_S
 224    while True:
 225        shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)
 226        if not _exists(path) or time.monotonic() > deadline:
 227            return
 228        time.sleep(0.05)
 229
 230
 231def _unlink(path: Path) -> None:
 232    try:
 233        path.unlink()
 234    except OSError:
 235        pass
 236
 237
 238def _place(source: Path, target: Path, token: str) -> bool:
 239    """Link ``source`` to ``target`` only if ``target`` does not exist; True when ``target`` carries ``token``.
 240
 241    The read-back covers a retransmitted link that landed but reported ``EEXIST``.
 242    """
 243    try:
 244        os.link(source, target)
 245        return True
 246    except OSError:
 247        held = _read_json(target)
 248        return isinstance(held, dict) and held.get("placed") == token
 249
 250
 251def _tmp_name(kind: str, token: str) -> str:
 252    """A ``tmp/`` entry name: its kind, the local time in milliseconds (for reading only) and a token."""
 253    return f"{kind}-{int(_now() * 1000)}-{token}"

 256@dataclass(frozen=True)
 257class Item:
 258    """One unit of work.
 259
 260    Attributes:
 261        id: Unique within the pool; matches :data:`ID_PATTERN`.
 262        resource_class: A name the caller defines; workers claim the classes they name.
 263        command: The argv the worker runs.
 264        env: Extra environment for the command.
 265        attempt: This run's attempt number, from 1; every failure, release and reap adds one.
 266        max_attempts: Failed attempts allowed (the pool's ``max_attempts`` when None).
 267        payload_sha256: sha256 of id, class, command and env (filled by :meth:`WorkPool.publish`).
 268    """
 269
 270    id: str
 271    resource_class: str
 272    command: Sequence[str]
 273    env: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
 274    attempt: int = 1
 275    max_attempts: Optional[int] = None
 276    payload_sha256: str = ""
 277
 278    def payload_digest(self) -> str:
 279        """The sha256 of the item's id, class, command and env."""
 280        payload = {
 281            "id": self.id,
 282            "resource_class": self.resource_class,
 283            "command": list(self.command),
 284            "env": dict(self.env),
 285        }
 286        return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()).hexdigest()
 287
 288    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
 289        """The item as JSON-ready data."""
 290        return {
 291            "id": self.id,
 292            "resource_class": self.resource_class,
 293            "command": list(self.command),
 294            "env": dict(self.env),
 295            "attempt": self.attempt,
 296            "max_attempts": self.max_attempts,
 297            "payload_sha256": self.payload_sha256,
 298        }
 299
 300    @classmethod
 301    def from_dict(cls, data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Item:
 302        """An item from :meth:`to_dict` data (other keys are ignored)."""
 303        return cls(
 304            id=data["id"],
 305            resource_class=data["resource_class"],
 306            command=tuple(data["command"]),
 307            env=dict(data.get("env") or {}),
 308            attempt=int(data.get("attempt", 1)),
 309            max_attempts=data.get("max_attempts"),
 310            payload_sha256=data.get("payload_sha256", ""),
 311        )
 312

 316    """A claimed item, held by one worker until it completes, fails, releases or loses it.
 317
 318    Attributes:
 319        item: The item, with this run's attempt number.

 321        worker: The claiming worker's name.
 322        path: ``leases/<item>``.
 323    """

 328    path: Path
