class WorkPool: 
332class WorkPool:
333    """A pool directory: publish, claim, heartbeat, complete, fail, release, reap and count items."""
334
335    def __init__(self, path: PathLike) -> None:
336        """Open an existing pool.
337
338        Args:
339            path: The pool directory (made by :meth:`create`).
340
341        Raises:
342            ValueError: There is no ``work-pool-1`` pool there.
343        """
344        self.root = Path(path).absolute()
345        cfg = _read_json(self.root / "pool.json")
346        if not isinstance(cfg, dict) or cfg.get("schema") != SCHEMA:
347            raise ValueError(f"{self.root} is not a {SCHEMA} pool")
348        self.lease_s = float(cfg["lease_s"])
349        self.heartbeat_s = float(cfg["heartbeat_s"])
350        self.max_attempts = int(cfg["max_attempts"])
351        self.max_interrupts = int(cfg["max_interrupts"])
352        self.success_codes = tuple(int(c) for c in cfg["success_codes"])
353        self.host = _host()
354        self._classes: dict[str, str] = {}
355
356    @classmethod
357    def create(
358        cls,
359        path: PathLike,
360        *,
361        lease_s: float,
362        heartbeat_s: float,
363        max_attempts: int = DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
364        max_interrupts: int = DEFAULT_MAX_INTERRUPTS,
365        success_codes: Sequence[int] = (0,),
366    ) -> WorkPool:
367        """Create a pool, or open it when it exists with the same settings.
368
369        Args:
370            path: The pool directory, on storage every worker's node can see.
371            lease_s: Seconds without a heartbeat after which a lease is reaped.
372            heartbeat_s: Seconds between a worker's heartbeats; at most a third of ``lease_s``.
373            max_attempts: Failed attempts an item may have (each item may set its own).
374            max_interrupts: Releases and reaps an item may have.
375            success_codes: Exit codes that complete an item.
376
377        Returns:
378            The pool.
379
380        Raises:
381            ValueError: A setting is out of range, or the pool exists with other settings.
382        """
383        if heartbeat_s <= 0 or lease_s < 3 * heartbeat_s:
384            raise ValueError("lease_s must be at least three heartbeats, and heartbeat_s positive")
385        if max_attempts < 1 or max_interrupts < 1:
386            raise ValueError("max_attempts and max_interrupts must be at least 1")
387        root = Path(path).absolute()
388        cfg = {
389            "schema": SCHEMA,
390            "lease_s": float(lease_s),
391            "heartbeat_s": float(heartbeat_s),
392            "max_attempts": int(max_attempts),
393            "max_interrupts": int(max_interrupts),
394            "success_codes": [int(c) for c in success_codes],
395        }
396        root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
397        for name in SUBDIRS:
398            (root / name).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
399        old = _read_json(root / "pool.json")
400        if old is None:
401            _write_json(root / "pool.json", cfg)
402        elif old != cfg:
403            keys = sorted(k for k in set(old) | set(cfg) if old.get(k) != cfg.get(k))
404            raise ValueError(f"{root}/pool.json exists with other settings: {keys}")
405        return cls(root)
406
407    def _d(self, name: str) -> Path:
408        return self.root / name
409
410    # -- clock and ages -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
411    def _server_now(self) -> float:
412        """The storage's clock: the mtime of a dot-file in ``tmp/`` just touched (a server time on NFS)."""
413        path = self._d("tmp") / f".clock-{self.host}-{os.getpid()}-{threading.get_ident()}"
414        os.close(os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT, 0o660))
415        try:
416            os.utime(path)
417            stamp = _fresh_mtime(path)
418        finally:
419            try:
420                path.unlink()
421            except OSError:
422                pass
423        return _now() if stamp is None else stamp
424
425    def _entry_time(self, path: Path) -> Optional[float]:
426        """When a ``tmp/`` entry last changed: the later of its mtime and ctime (storage clock)."""
427        return _fresh_times(path)
428
429    # -- publishing ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
430    def _tmp_items(self) -> list[tuple[Path, dict[str, Any]]]:
431        """Items held in ``tmp/``: staged claims, hand-offs and publish files."""
432        held = []
433        for name in _names(self._d("tmp")):
434            path = self._d("tmp") / name
435            for candidate in (path, path / "item.json", path / NEXT):
436                data = _read_json(candidate) if candidate != path or name.endswith(".json") else None
437                if isinstance(data, dict) and "id" in data:
438                    held.append((path, data))
439        return held
440
441    def _known(self, item_id: str) -> bool:
442        if any(
443            _exists(p)
444            for p in (
445                self._d("queue") / f"{item_id}.json",
446                self._d("leases") / item_id,
447                self._d("done") / f"{item_id}.json",
448                self._d("dead") / f"{item_id}.json",
449            )
450        ):
451            return True
452        return any(data.get("id") == item_id for _, data in self._tmp_items())
453
454    def publish(self, items: Iterable[Item]) -> list[Item]:
455        """Put items in the queue, each with one exclusive ``link(2)`` from ``tmp/``.
456
457        Every item is checked before any is published. An id that appears in the queue between the check and the
458        link raises; the items before it stay published.
459
460        Args:
461            items: New items; their ids must not be in the pool yet.
462
463        Returns:
464            The published items, with ``payload_sha256`` and ``max_attempts`` filled in.
465
466        Raises:
467            ValueError: An item is malformed, repeats an id, or is already in the pool.
468        """
469        ready: list[Item] = []
470        seen: set[str] = set()
471        for item in items:
472            if not ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(item.id):
473                raise ValueError(f"item id {item.id!r} does not match {ID_PATTERN.pattern}")
474            if not item.resource_class or not item.command or item.attempt < 1:
475                raise ValueError(f"item {item.id} needs a resource class, a command and an attempt >= 1")
476            if not all(isinstance(a, str) for a in item.command) or not all(
477                isinstance(k, str) and isinstance(v, str) for k, v in item.env.items()
478            ):
479                raise ValueError(f"item {item.id}: command and env must be strings")
480            if item.id in seen or self._known(item.id):
481                raise ValueError(f"item {item.id} is already in the pool")
482            digest = item.payload_digest()
483            if item.payload_sha256 and item.payload_sha256 != digest:
484                raise ValueError(f"item {item.id}: payload_sha256 does not match its payload")
485            seen.add(item.id)
486            ready.append(
487                replace(
488                    item,
489                    command=tuple(item.command),
490                    env=dict(item.env),
491                    max_attempts=item.max_attempts or self.max_attempts,
492                    payload_sha256=digest,
493                )
494            )
495        for item in ready:
496            token = uuid.uuid4().hex
497            staged = self._d("tmp") / (_tmp_name("pub", token) + ".json")
498            staged.write_text(json.dumps({**item.to_dict(), "placed": token}, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
499            try:
500                if not _place(staged, self._d("queue") / f"{item.id}.json", token):
501                    raise ValueError(f"item {item.id} is already in the pool")
502            finally:
503                _unlink(staged)
504        return ready
505
506    # -- claiming ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
507    def _class_of(self, item_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
508        cls = self._classes.get(item_id)
509        if cls is None:
510            data = _read_json(self._d("queue") / f"{item_id}.json")
511            if not isinstance(data, dict):
512                return None
513            cls = self._classes[item_id] = str(data["resource_class"])
514        return cls
515
516    def _stage(self, worker: str) -> tuple[Path, str, float]:
517        """A complete claim directory (owner.json, heartbeat) in ``tmp/``, not yet holding an item."""
518        token = uuid.uuid4().hex
519        staged = self._d("tmp") / _tmp_name("claim", token)
520        staged.mkdir()
521        _write_json(
522            staged / "owner.json",
523            {"token": token, "worker": worker, "host": self.host, "pid": os.getpid(), "claimed": _now()},
524        )
525        (staged / "heartbeat").touch()
526        return staged, token, time.monotonic()
527
528    def _conflict(self, held_item: Path, item_id: str, reason: str, token: str) -> None:
529        """Move an item that must not run (a duplicate) to ``conflicts/``."""
530        try:
531            os.rename(held_item, self._d("conflicts") / f"{item_id}.{reason}.{token[:12]}.json")
532        except OSError:
533            pass  # left where it is: reap() settles it, and _settle drops a superseded copy
534
535    def _try_claim(self, staged: Path, token: str, item_id: str, worker: str) -> tuple[Optional[Lease], bool]:
536        """Take one item into the staged dir, then publish the lease. Returns (lease, staged dir still usable)."""
537        source, held_item = self._d("queue") / f"{item_id}.json", staged / "item.json"
538        try:
539            os.rename(source, held_item)
540        except OSError:
541            pass  # usually another worker took it; a retransmitted rename that landed is caught by the read-back
542        data = _read_json(held_item)
543        if not isinstance(data, dict):
544            return None, _exists(staged)
545        item = Item.from_dict(data)
546        for reason in ("done", "dead"):
547            if _exists(self._d(reason) / f"{item.id}.json"):
548                self._conflict(held_item, item.id, reason, token)
549                return None, not _exists(held_item)
550        try:
551            _write_json(
552                staged / "owner.json",
553                {
554                    "token": token,
555                    "worker": worker,
556                    "host": self.host,
557                    "pid": os.getpid(),
558                    "claimed": _now(),
559                    "item": item.id,
560                    "attempt": item.attempt,
561                },
562            )
563            (staged / "attempt").write_text(f"{item.attempt}\n")
564            os.utime(staged / "heartbeat")
565        except OSError:
566            return None, False  # the staged dir was reaped under a stalled claim; the reaper requeues the item
567        target = self._d("leases") / item.id
568        error: Optional[OSError] = None
569        try:
570            os.rename(staged, target)
571        except OSError as exc:
572            error = exc
573        held = _read_json(target / "owner.json")
574        if isinstance(held, dict) and held.get("token") == token:
575            return Lease(item=item, token=token, worker=worker, path=target), False
576        if error is not None and error.errno in (errno.ENOTEMPTY, errno.EEXIST):
577            self._conflict(held_item, item.id, "leased", token)  # a lease of this id exists: a duplicate
578            return None, not _exists(held_item)
579        try:
580            os.rename(held_item, source)  # give the item back
581        except OSError:
582            pass  # the staged dir was reaped (or the rename failed): reap() returns the item after lease_s
583        return None, False
584
585    def claim(self, resource_classes: Iterable[str], worker: str) -> Optional[Lease]:
586        """Reap, then claim one queued item of the given classes.
587
588        An item that already has a ``done/`` or ``dead/`` record, or whose lease dir already exists, is a duplicate:
589        it goes to ``conflicts/`` instead of running.
590
591        Args:
592            resource_classes: The classes this worker can run.
593            worker: The worker's name, recorded in the lease.
594
595        Returns:
596            The lease, or None when no item of those classes could be claimed.
597        """
598        classes = set(resource_classes)
599        self.reap()
600        staged: Optional[Path] = None
601        token, made = "", 0.0
602        try:
603            for name in sorted(_names(self._d("queue"))):
604                if not name.endswith(".json"):
605                    continue
606                item_id = name[: -len(".json")]
607                if self._class_of(item_id) not in classes:
608                    continue
609                if staged is not None and time.monotonic() - made > self.lease_s / 2:
610                    self._drop_staged(staged)
611                    staged = None
612                if staged is None:
613                    staged, token, made = self._stage(worker)
614                lease, usable = self._try_claim(staged, token, item_id, worker)
615                if lease is not None:
616                    staged = None
617                    return lease
618                if not usable:
619                    self._drop_staged(staged)
620                    staged = None
621            return None
622        finally:
623            if staged is not None:
624                self._drop_staged(staged)
625
626    def _drop_staged(self, staged: Path) -> None:
627        """Remove a staged claim dir unless it holds an item, which reap() then returns to the queue."""
628        if not _exists(staged / "item.json"):
629            shutil.rmtree(staged, ignore_errors=True)
630
631    def _still_mine(self, lease: Lease) -> bool:
632        """Whether the lease is the caller's: a token mismatch says no at once.
633
634        Absence is re-checked once after :data:`PUTBACK_WAIT_S`, because a reaper that renamed a live lease aside
635        puts it back.
636        """
637        for check in range(2):
638            held = _read_json(lease.path / "owner.json")
639            if isinstance(held, dict):
640                return held.get("token") == lease.token
641            if check == 0:
642                time.sleep(PUTBACK_WAIT_S)
643        return False
644
645    def heartbeat(self, lease: Lease) -> bool:
646        """Touch the lease's heartbeat if the lease is still this caller's.
647
648        Args:
649            lease: The lease.
650
651        Returns:
652            False when the lease was lost: another token holds it, or it was absent on two checks.
653        """
654        for check in range(2):
655            if not self._still_mine(lease):
656                return False
657            try:
658                os.utime(lease.path / "heartbeat")
659                return True
660            except OSError as exc:
661                if not _gone(exc):
662                    raise
663        return False
664
665    # -- finishing -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
666    def _take_lease(self, lease: Lease, kind: str) -> Optional[Path]:
667        """Rename the caller's lease aside into ``tmp/``; None when it is no longer the caller's."""
668        for check in range(2):
669            if not self._still_mine(lease):
670                return None
671            aside = self._d("tmp") / _tmp_name(kind, lease.token)
672            try:
673                os.rename(lease.path, aside)
674            except OSError:
675                pass  # read back below
676            held = _read_json(aside / "owner.json")
677            if not isinstance(held, dict):
678                continue  # gone between the check and the rename (a reaper's put-back window): check again
679            if held.get("token") != lease.token:  # reaped and claimed again between the check and the rename
680                try:
681                    os.rename(aside, lease.path)
682                except OSError:
683                    pass  # left in tmp/: reap() settles it after lease_s
684                return None
685            _mark_moved(aside)
686            return aside
687        return None
688
689    def _superseded(self, item: Item, aside: Path) -> bool:
690        """Whether a newer copy of the item exists outside this aside dir (so this one is a leftover).
691
692        Checked in the order an item moves (queue, tmp, leases, dead), so a copy moving on is still seen.
693        """
694        if _exists(self._d("queue") / f"{item.id}.json"):
695            return True
696        for path, data in self._tmp_items():
697            if path != aside and data.get("id") == item.id and int(data.get("attempt", 0)) > item.attempt:
698                return True
699        return _exists(self._d("leases") / item.id / "item.json") or _exists(self._d("dead") / f"{item.id}.json")
700
701    def _settle(self, aside: Path, kind: str, record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
702        """Record an interrupted or failed attempt, then requeue the item with attempt+1 or bury it in dead/.
703
704        The next state is written to a new file in the aside dir and linked into place last, so a crash at any
705        point leaves ``item.json`` unchanged for the next reaper, which re-derives the same attempt number.
706
707        Returns ``requeued``, ``dead``, ``done`` (it had completed; dropped), ``superseded`` (a leftover copy;
708        dropped), or ``lost`` (another process took the aside dir).
709        """
710        data = _read_json(aside / "item.json")
711        if not isinstance(data, dict):
712            _remove_dir(aside)
713            return "lost"
714        item = Item.from_dict(data)
715        if _exists(self._d("done") / f"{item.id}.json"):
716            _remove_dir(aside)
717            return "done"
718        if self._superseded(item, aside):
719            _remove_dir(aside)
720            return "superseded"
721        directory = self._d(kind)
722        token = uuid.uuid4().hex
723        try:
724            _write_json(
725                directory / f"{item.id}.{item.attempt}.json",
726                {
727                    **record,
728                    "id": item.id,
729                    "attempt": item.attempt,
730                    "resource_class": item.resource_class,
731                    "host": self.host,
732                    "time": _now(),
733                },
734            )
735            count = sum(_exists(directory / f"{item.id}.{a}.json") for a in range(1, item.attempt + 1))
736            limit = (item.max_attempts or self.max_attempts) if kind == "failed" else self.max_interrupts
737            if count >= limit:
738                reason = "failures" if kind == "failed" else "interrupts"
739                following = {**item.to_dict(), "dead_reason": reason, "dead_time": _now()}
740                outcome, target = "dead", self._d("dead") / f"{item.id}.json"
741            else:
742                following = replace(item, attempt=item.attempt + 1).to_dict()
743                outcome, target = "requeued", self._d("queue") / f"{item.id}.json"
744            _write_json(aside / NEXT, {**following, "placed": token})
745        except OSError:
746            return "lost"
747        if not _place(aside / NEXT, target, token):
748            return "lost"
749        _remove_dir(aside)
750        return outcome
751
752    def complete(self, lease: Lease, result: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
753        """Mark the lease's item done: ``done/<item>.json`` holds ``result`` plus the item, attempt, worker and host.
754
755        Args:
756            lease: The caller's lease.
757            result: What to record, e.g. ``exit_code``, ``start``, ``end``.
758
759        Returns:
760            False, writing nothing, when the lease is no longer the caller's (so a second call is a no-op).
761        """
762        aside = self._take_lease(lease, "done")
763        if aside is None:
764            return False
765        item = lease.item
766        record = {
767            **result,
768            "id": item.id,
769            "attempt": item.attempt,
770            "resource_class": item.resource_class,
771            "worker": lease.worker,
772            "host": self.host,
773            "token": lease.token,
774            "completed": _now(),
775            "placed": lease.token,
776        }
777        try:
778            _write_json(aside / "done.json", record)
779        except OSError:
780            return False
781        if not _place(aside / "done.json", self._d("done") / f"{item.id}.json", lease.token):
782            return False
783        _remove_dir(aside)
784        return True
785
786    def fail(self, lease: Lease, exit_code: int) -> str:
787        """Record a failed attempt; requeue the item with attempt+1, or send it to ``dead/`` once its budget is spent.
788
789        Args:
790            lease: The caller's lease.
791            exit_code: The command's exit code.
792
793        Returns:
794            ``retry``, ``dead``, or ``lost`` (the lease is no longer the caller's; nothing written).
795        """
796        aside = self._take_lease(lease, "fail")
797        if aside is None:
798            return "lost"
799        outcome = self._settle(aside, "failed", {"exit_code": int(exit_code), "worker": lease.worker})
800        return {"requeued": "retry", "dead": "dead"}.get(outcome, "lost")
801
802    def release(self, lease: Lease) -> str:
803        """Give the item back without spending a retry; its attempt still goes up and counts toward max_interrupts.
804
805        Args:
806            lease: The caller's lease.
807
808        Returns:
809            ``requeued``, ``dead`` (``max_interrupts`` reached), or ``lost`` (nothing written).
810        """
811        aside = self._take_lease(lease, "release")
812        if aside is None:
813            return "lost"
814        outcome = self._settle(aside, "interrupted", {"reason": "release", "worker": lease.worker})
815        return outcome if outcome in ("requeued", "dead") else "lost"
816
817    # -- reaping -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
818    def _beat(self, lease_dir: Path) -> Optional[float]:
819        for name in ("heartbeat", "owner.json", "item.json"):
820            mtime = _fresh_mtime(lease_dir / name)
821            if mtime is not None:
822                return mtime
823        return None
824
825    def _settle_reaped(self, aside: Path) -> int:
826        _mark_moved(aside)
827        owner = _read_json(aside / "owner.json")
828        outcome = self._settle(aside, "interrupted", {"reason": "reap", "previous_owner": owner})
829        return 1 if outcome in ("requeued", "dead") else 0
830
831    def _reap_lease(self, item_id: str, now: float) -> int:
832        """Reap one lease whose heartbeat is older than lease_s; only one reaper wins the rename aside.
833
834        The owner's token is read before the rename and the heartbeat is checked again after it; a lease that
835        turns out to be another or a fresh one is put back.
836        """
837        lease_dir = self._d("leases") / item_id
838        held = _read_json(lease_dir / "owner.json")
839        token = held.get("token") if isinstance(held, dict) else None
840        beat = self._beat(lease_dir)
841        if token is None or beat is None or now - beat <= self.lease_s:
842            return 0
843        aside = self._d("tmp") / _tmp_name("reap", uuid.uuid4().hex)
844        try:
845            os.rename(lease_dir, aside)
846        except OSError:
847            pass  # read back below
848        if not _exists(aside):
849            return 0
850        moved = _read_json(aside / "owner.json")
851        beat = self._beat(aside)
852        mine = isinstance(moved, dict) and moved.get("token") == token
853        if not mine or beat is None or self._server_now() - beat <= self.lease_s:
854            try:
855                os.rename(aside, lease_dir)  # another lease took the name, or this one is fresh: put it back
856                return 0
857            except OSError:
858                pass
859        return self._settle_reaped(aside)
860
861    def reap(self) -> int:
862        """Re-publish expired leases and abandoned ``tmp/`` entries (older than lease_s) with attempt+1.
863
864        Ages are measured on the storage's clock (heartbeat mtimes against a just-touched file), so a node whose
865        clock is off neither reaps live leases nor keeps dead ones. Each reap counts as an interruption, so an
866        item reaped ``max_interrupts`` times goes to ``dead/`` instead.
867
868        Returns:
869            How many items this call re-published or sent to ``dead/``.
870        """
871        now = self._server_now()
872        count = sum(self._reap_lease(name, now) for name in _names(self._d("leases")))
873        for name in _names(self._d("tmp")):
874            path = self._d("tmp") / name
875            changed = self._entry_time(path)
876            if changed is None or now - changed <= self.lease_s:
877                continue
878            if name.endswith(".json"):  # a publish file whose publisher stalled or died
879                _unlink(path)
880                continue
881            aside = self._d("tmp") / _tmp_name("reap", uuid.uuid4().hex)
882            try:
883                os.rename(path, aside)
884            except OSError:
885                pass
886            if _exists(aside):
887                count += self._settle_reaped(aside)
888        return count
889
890    # -- host checks ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
891    def note_host_check_failure(self, worker: str, partition: Optional[str], rc: Union[int, str]) -> None:
892        """Record that a worker on ``partition`` failed its host check.
893
894        Args:
895            worker: The worker's name.
896            partition: The worker's partition (``SLURM_JOB_PARTITION``); None outside Slurm.
897            rc: The check's exit code, or ``timeout``.
898        """
899        directory = self._d("hostcheck")
900        directory.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
901        part = partition or ""
902        safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", part) or "_"
903        _write_json(
904            directory / f"{safe}.{worker}.{int(_now() * 1000)}.json",
905            {"partition": part, "worker": worker, "host": self.host, "rc": rc},
906        )
907
908    def host_check_failures(self, window_s: float) -> dict[str, int]:
909        """Host-check failures per partition recorded within the last ``window_s`` seconds (storage clock)."""
910        now = self._server_now()
911        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
912        for name in _names(self._d("hostcheck")):
913            path = self._d("hostcheck") / name
914            changed = _fresh_mtime(path)
915            record = _read_json(path)
916            if changed is None or now - changed > window_s or not isinstance(record, dict):
917                continue
918            part = str(record.get("partition") or "")
919            if part:
920                counts[part] = counts.get(part, 0) + 1
921        return counts
922
923    # -- counting ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
924    def status(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
925        """Counts per state and per class, also written to ``status.json``.
926
927        Returns:
928            ``{"schema", "time", "counts": {queued, leased, done, dead, failed_attempts, interrupted, staged,
929            conflicts}, "classes": {class: {queued, leased, done, dead}}, "workers"}``.
930        """
931        per_class: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
932
933        def add(state: str, data: Any) -> None:  # noqa: ANN401
934            if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("resource_class"):
935                row = per_class.setdefault(
936                    str(data["resource_class"]), {"queued": 0, "leased": 0, "done": 0, "dead": 0}
937                )
938                row[state] += 1
939
940        queued = [n for n in _names(self._d("queue")) if n.endswith(".json")]
941        leased = _names(self._d("leases"))
942        done = [n for n in _names(self._d("done")) if n.endswith(".json")]
943        dead = [n for n in _names(self._d("dead")) if n.endswith(".json")]
944        for name in queued:
945            add("queued", _read_json(self._d("queue") / name))
946        for name in leased:
947            add("leased", _read_json(self._d("leases") / name / "item.json"))
948        for name in done:
949            add("done", _read_json(self._d("done") / name))
950        for name in dead:
951            add("dead", _read_json(self._d("dead") / name))
952        staged = sum(_exists(self._d("tmp") / n / "item.json") for n in _names(self._d("tmp")))
953        result = {
954            "schema": SCHEMA,
955            "time": _now(),
956            "counts": {
957                "queued": len(queued),
958                "leased": len(leased),
959                "done": len(done),
960                "dead": len(dead),
961                "failed_attempts": len(_names(self._d("failed"))),
962                "interrupted": len(_names(self._d("interrupted"))),
963                "staged": staged,
964                "conflicts": len(_names(self._d("conflicts"))),
965            },
966            "classes": per_class,
967            "workers": len(_names(self._d("workers"))),
968        }
969        _write_json(self.root / "status.json", result)
970        return result

A pool directory: publish, claim, heartbeat, complete, fail, release, reap and count items.

335    def __init__(self, path: PathLike) -> None:
336        """Open an existing pool.

@classmethod
def create( cls, path: Union[str, pathlib.Path], *, lease_s: float, heartbeat_s: float, max_attempts: int = 2, max_interrupts: int = 6, success_codes: Sequence[int] = (0,)) -> WorkPool: 
356    @classmethod
357    def create(
358        cls,
359        path: PathLike,
360        *,
361        lease_s: float,
362        heartbeat_s: float,
363        max_attempts: int = DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
364        max_interrupts: int = DEFAULT_MAX_INTERRUPTS,
365        success_codes: Sequence[int] = (0,),
366    ) -> WorkPool:
367        """Create a pool, or open it when it exists with the same settings.
368
369        Args:
370            path: The pool directory, on storage every worker's node can see.
371            lease_s: Seconds without a heartbeat after which a lease is reaped.
372            heartbeat_s: Seconds between a worker's heartbeats; at most a third of ``lease_s``.
373            max_attempts: Failed attempts an item may have (each item may set its own).
374            max_interrupts: Releases and reaps an item may have.
375            success_codes: Exit codes that complete an item.
376
377        Returns:
378            The pool.
379
380        Raises:
381            ValueError: A setting is out of range, or the pool exists with other settings.
382        """
383        if heartbeat_s <= 0 or lease_s < 3 * heartbeat_s:
384            raise ValueError("lease_s must be at least three heartbeats, and heartbeat_s positive")
385        if max_attempts < 1 or max_interrupts < 1:
386            raise ValueError("max_attempts and max_interrupts must be at least 1")
387        root = Path(path).absolute()
388        cfg = {
389            "schema": SCHEMA,
390            "lease_s": float(lease_s),
391            "heartbeat_s": float(heartbeat_s),
392            "max_attempts": int(max_attempts),
393            "max_interrupts": int(max_interrupts),
394            "success_codes": [int(c) for c in success_codes],
395        }
396        root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
397        for name in SUBDIRS:
398            (root / name).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
399        old = _read_json(root / "pool.json")
400        if old is None:
401            _write_json(root / "pool.json", cfg)
402        elif old != cfg:
403            keys = sorted(k for k in set(old) | set(cfg) if old.get(k) != cfg.get(k))
404            raise ValueError(f"{root}/pool.json exists with other settings: {keys}")
405        return cls(root)

  • max_attempts: Failed attempts an item may have (each item may set its own).

Raises:

def publish( self, items: Iterable[Item]) -> list[Item]: 
454    def publish(self, items: Iterable[Item]) -> list[Item]:
455        """Put items in the queue, each with one exclusive ``link(2)`` from ``tmp/``.
456
457        Every item is checked before any is published. An id that appears in the queue between the check and the
458        link raises; the items before it stay published.
459
460        Args:
461            items: New items; their ids must not be in the pool yet.
462
463        Returns:
464            The published items, with ``payload_sha256`` and ``max_attempts`` filled in.
465
466        Raises:
467            ValueError: An item is malformed, repeats an id, or is already in the pool.
468        """
469        ready: list[Item] = []
470        seen: set[str] = set()
471        for item in items:
472            if not ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(item.id):
473                raise ValueError(f"item id {item.id!r} does not match {ID_PATTERN.pattern}")
474            if not item.resource_class or not item.command or item.attempt < 1:
475                raise ValueError(f"item {item.id} needs a resource class, a command and an attempt >= 1")
476            if not all(isinstance(a, str) for a in item.command) or not all(
477                isinstance(k, str) and isinstance(v, str) for k, v in item.env.items()
478            ):
479                raise ValueError(f"item {item.id}: command and env must be strings")
480            if item.id in seen or self._known(item.id):
481                raise ValueError(f"item {item.id} is already in the pool")
482            digest = item.payload_digest()
483            if item.payload_sha256 and item.payload_sha256 != digest:
484                raise ValueError(f"item {item.id}: payload_sha256 does not match its payload")
485            seen.add(item.id)
486            ready.append(
487                replace(
488                    item,
489                    command=tuple(item.command),
490                    env=dict(item.env),
491                    max_attempts=item.max_attempts or self.max_attempts,
492                    payload_sha256=digest,
493                )
494            )
495        for item in ready:
496            token = uuid.uuid4().hex
497            staged = self._d("tmp") / (_tmp_name("pub", token) + ".json")
498            staged.write_text(json.dumps({**item.to_dict(), "placed": token}, indent=1, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
499            try:
500                if not _place(staged, self._d("queue") / f"{item.id}.json", token):
501                    raise ValueError(f"item {item.id} is already in the pool")
502            finally:
503                _unlink(staged)
504        return ready

Put items in the queue, each with one exclusive link(2) from tmp/.

Every item is checked before any is published. An id that appears in the queue between the check and the link raises; the items before it stay published.

Arguments:
  • items: New items; their ids must not be in the pool yet.
Returns:

The published items, with payload_sha256 and max_attempts filled in.

Raises:
  • ValueError: An item is malformed, repeats an id, or is already in the pool.
def claim( self, resource_classes: Iterable[str], worker: str) -> Optional[Lease]: 
585    def claim(self, resource_classes: Iterable[str], worker: str) -> Optional[Lease]:
586        """Reap, then claim one queued item of the given classes.
587
588        An item that already has a ``done/`` or ``dead/`` record, or whose lease dir already exists, is a duplicate:
589        it goes to ``conflicts/`` instead of running.
590
591        Args:
592            resource_classes: The classes this worker can run.
593            worker: The worker's name, recorded in the lease.
594
595        Returns:
596            The lease, or None when no item of those classes could be claimed.
597        """
598        classes = set(resource_classes)
599        self.reap()
600        staged: Optional[Path] = None
601        token, made = "", 0.0
602        try:
603            for name in sorted(_names(self._d("queue"))):
604                if not name.endswith(".json"):
605                    continue
606                item_id = name[: -len(".json")]
607                if self._class_of(item_id) not in classes:
608                    continue
609                if staged is not None and time.monotonic() - made > self.lease_s / 2:
610                    self._drop_staged(staged)
611                    staged = None
612                if staged is None:
613                    staged, token, made = self._stage(worker)
614                lease, usable = self._try_claim(staged, token, item_id, worker)
615                if lease is not None:
616                    staged = None
617                    return lease
618                if not usable:
619                    self._drop_staged(staged)
620                    staged = None
621            return None
622        finally:
623            if staged is not None:
624                self._drop_staged(staged)

Arguments:

Returns:

The lease, or None when no item of those classes could be claimed.

def heartbeat(self, lease: Lease) -> bool: 
645    def heartbeat(self, lease: Lease) -> bool:
646        """Touch the lease's heartbeat if the lease is still this caller's.
647
648        Args:
649            lease: The lease.
650
651        Returns:
652            False when the lease was lost: another token holds it, or it was absent on two checks.
653        """
654        for check in range(2):
655            if not self._still_mine(lease):
656                return False
657            try:
658                os.utime(lease.path / "heartbeat")
659                return True
660            except OSError as exc:
661                if not _gone(exc):
662                    raise
663        return False

Touch the lease's heartbeat if the lease is still this caller's.

Arguments:

def complete( self, lease: Lease, result: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool: 
752    def complete(self, lease: Lease, result: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool:
753        """Mark the lease's item done: ``done/<item>.json`` holds ``result`` plus the item, attempt, worker and host.
754
755        Args:
756            lease: The caller's lease.
757            result: What to record, e.g. ``exit_code``, ``start``, ``end``.
758
759        Returns:
760            False, writing nothing, when the lease is no longer the caller's (so a second call is a no-op).
761        """
762        aside = self._take_lease(lease, "done")
763        if aside is None:
764            return False
765        item = lease.item
766        record = {
767            **result,
768            "id": item.id,
769            "attempt": item.attempt,
770            "resource_class": item.resource_class,
771            "worker": lease.worker,
772            "host": self.host,
773            "token": lease.token,
774            "completed": _now(),
775            "placed": lease.token,
776        }
777        try:
778            _write_json(aside / "done.json", record)
779        except OSError:
780            return False
781        if not _place(aside / "done.json", self._d("done") / f"{item.id}.json", lease.token):
782            return False
783        _remove_dir(aside)
784        return True

Arguments:

False, writing nothing, when the lease is no longer the caller's (so a second call is a no-op).

def fail(self, lease: Lease, exit_code: int) -> str: 
786    def fail(self, lease: Lease, exit_code: int) -> str:
787        """Record a failed attempt; requeue the item with attempt+1, or send it to ``dead/`` once its budget is spent.
788
789        Args:
790            lease: The caller's lease.
791            exit_code: The command's exit code.
792
793        Returns:
794            ``retry``, ``dead``, or ``lost`` (the lease is no longer the caller's; nothing written).
795        """
796        aside = self._take_lease(lease, "fail")
797        if aside is None:
798            return "lost"
799        outcome = self._settle(aside, "failed", {"exit_code": int(exit_code), "worker": lease.worker})
800        return {"requeued": "retry", "dead": "dead"}.get(outcome, "lost")

Record a failed attempt; requeue the item with attempt+1, or send it to dead/ once its budget is spent.

Arguments:
  • lease: The caller's lease.
  • exit_code: The command's exit code.
Returns:

retry, dead, or lost (the lease is no longer the caller's; nothing written).

def release(self, lease: Lease) -> str: 
802    def release(self, lease: Lease) -> str:
803        """Give the item back without spending a retry; its attempt still goes up and counts toward max_interrupts.
804
805        Args:
806            lease: The caller's lease.
807
808        Returns:
809            ``requeued``, ``dead`` (``max_interrupts`` reached), or ``lost`` (nothing written).
810        """
811        aside = self._take_lease(lease, "release")
812        if aside is None:
813            return "lost"
814        outcome = self._settle(aside, "interrupted", {"reason": "release", "worker": lease.worker})
815        return outcome if outcome in ("requeued", "dead") else "lost"

Give the item back without spending a retry; its attempt still goes up and counts toward max_interrupts.

Arguments:
  • lease: The caller's lease.
Returns:

requeued, dead (max_interrupts reached), or lost (nothing written).

def reap(self) -> int: 
861    def reap(self) -> int:
862        """Re-publish expired leases and abandoned ``tmp/`` entries (older than lease_s) with attempt+1.
863
864        Ages are measured on the storage's clock (heartbeat mtimes against a just-touched file), so a node whose
865        clock is off neither reaps live leases nor keeps dead ones. Each reap counts as an interruption, so an
866        item reaped ``max_interrupts`` times goes to ``dead/`` instead.
867
868        Returns:
869            How many items this call re-published or sent to ``dead/``.
870        """
871        now = self._server_now()
872        count = sum(self._reap_lease(name, now) for name in _names(self._d("leases")))
873        for name in _names(self._d("tmp")):
874            path = self._d("tmp") / name
875            changed = self._entry_time(path)
876            if changed is None or now - changed <= self.lease_s:
877                continue
878            if name.endswith(".json"):  # a publish file whose publisher stalled or died
879                _unlink(path)
880                continue
881            aside = self._d("tmp") / _tmp_name("reap", uuid.uuid4().hex)
882            try:
883                os.rename(path, aside)
884            except OSError:
885                pass
886            if _exists(aside):
887                count += self._settle_reaped(aside)
888        return count

Re-publish expired leases and abandoned tmp/ entries (older than lease_s) with attempt+1.

Ages are measured on the storage's clock (heartbeat mtimes against a just-touched file), so a node whose clock is off neither reaps live leases nor keeps dead ones. Each reap counts as an interruption, so an item reaped max_interrupts times goes to dead/ instead.

Returns:

How many items this call re-published or sent to dead/.

def note_host_check_failure(self, worker: str, partition: Optional[str], rc: Union[int, str]) -> None: 
891    def note_host_check_failure(self, worker: str, partition: Optional[str], rc: Union[int, str]) -> None:
892        """Record that a worker on ``partition`` failed its host check.
893
894        Args:

896            partition: The worker's partition (``SLURM_JOB_PARTITION``); None outside Slurm.
897            rc: The check's exit code, or ``timeout``.
898        """
899        directory = self._d("hostcheck")

903        _write_json(

905            {"partition": part, "worker": worker, "host": self.host, "rc": rc},
906        )

def host_check_failures(self, window_s: float) -> dict[str, int]: 
908    def host_check_failures(self, window_s: float) -> dict[str, int]:
909        """Host-check failures per partition recorded within the last ``window_s`` seconds (storage clock)."""
910        now = self._server_now()
911        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
912        for name in _names(self._d("hostcheck")):
913            path = self._d("hostcheck") / name
914            changed = _fresh_mtime(path)
915            record = _read_json(path)
916            if changed is None or now - changed > window_s or not isinstance(record, dict):
917                continue
918            part = str(record.get("partition") or "")
919            if part:
920                counts[part] = counts.get(part, 0) + 1
921        return counts

def status(self) -> dict[str, typing.Any]: 
924    def status(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
925        """Counts per state and per class, also written to ``status.json``.
926
927        Returns:
928            ``{"schema", "time", "counts": {queued, leased, done, dead, failed_attempts, interrupted, staged,
929            conflicts}, "classes": {class: {queued, leased, done, dead}}, "workers"}``.
930        """
931        per_class: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
932
933        def add(state: str, data: Any) -> None:  # noqa: ANN401
934            if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("resource_class"):
935                row = per_class.setdefault(
936                    str(data["resource_class"]), {"queued": 0, "leased": 0, "done": 0, "dead": 0}
937                )
938                row[state] += 1
939
940        queued = [n for n in _names(self._d("queue")) if n.endswith(".json")]
941        leased = _names(self._d("leases"))
942        done = [n for n in _names(self._d("done")) if n.endswith(".json")]
943        dead = [n for n in _names(self._d("dead")) if n.endswith(".json")]
944        for name in queued:
945            add("queued", _read_json(self._d("queue") / name))
946        for name in leased:
947            add("leased", _read_json(self._d("leases") / name / "item.json"))
948        for name in done:
949            add("done", _read_json(self._d("done") / name))
950        for name in dead:
951            add("dead", _read_json(self._d("dead") / name))
952        staged = sum(_exists(self._d("tmp") / n / "item.json") for n in _names(self._d("tmp")))
953        result = {
954            "schema": SCHEMA,
955            "time": _now(),
956            "counts": {
957                "queued": len(queued),
958                "leased": len(leased),
959                "done": len(done),
960                "dead": len(dead),
961                "failed_attempts": len(_names(self._d("failed"))),
962                "interrupted": len(_names(self._d("interrupted"))),
963                "staged": staged,
964                "conflicts": len(_names(self._d("conflicts"))),
965            },
966            "classes": per_class,
967            "workers": len(_names(self._d("workers"))),
968        }
969        _write_json(self.root / "status.json", result)
970        return result

Counts per state and per class, also written to status.json.

Returns:

{"schema", "time", "counts": {queued, leased, done, dead, failed_attempts, interrupted, staged, conflicts}, "classes": {class: {queued, leased, done, dead}}, "workers"}.

def work( pool: Union[str, pathlib.Path], classes: Sequence[str], *, worker: Optional[str] = None, linger: int = 3, poll_s: float = 10.0, host_check: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None, host_check_timeout_s: float = 300.0) -> int: 
1152def work(
1153    pool: PathLike,
1154    classes: Sequence[str],
1155    *,
1156    worker: Optional[str] = None,
1157    linger: int = 3,
1158    poll_s: float = 10.0,
1159    host_check: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
1160    host_check_timeout_s: float = HOST_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S,
1161) -> int:
1162    """Run one worker in this process until the queue stays empty (installs SIGTERM and SIGINT handlers).
1163
1164    Args:
1165        pool: The pool directory.
1166        classes: The resource classes this worker claims.
1167        worker: The worker's name (default ``<host>-<job id or "local">-<pid>``).
1168        linger: Further empty polls before the worker exits.
1169        poll_s: Seconds between polls of an empty queue.
1170        host_check: A command run once, before the first claim; when it fails or outlasts
1171            ``host_check_timeout_s``, the worker records it under ``hostcheck/`` for its partition and exits with
1172            :data:`HOST_CHECK_EXIT` without claiming anything.
1173        host_check_timeout_s: Seconds the host check may run.
1174
1175    Returns:
1176        0, :data:`SIGNAL_EXIT` after SIGTERM or SIGINT, or :data:`HOST_CHECK_EXIT`.
1177    """
1178    name = worker or f"{_host()}-{os.environ.get('SLURM_JOB_ID', 'local')}-{os.getpid()}"
1179    name = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", name)
1180    return _Worker(WorkPool(pool), classes, name, linger, poll_s, host_check, host_check_timeout_s).loop()

Run one worker in this process until the queue stays empty (installs SIGTERM and SIGINT handlers).

Arguments:
  • pool: The pool directory.
  • classes: The resource classes this worker claims.
  • worker: The worker's name (default <host>-<job id or "local">-<pid>).
  • linger: Further empty polls before the worker exits.
  • poll_s: Seconds between polls of an empty queue.
  • host_check: A command run once, before the first claim; when it fails or outlasts host_check_timeout_s, the worker records it under hostcheck/ for its partition and exits with HOST_CHECK_EXIT without claiming anything.
  • host_check_timeout_s: Seconds the host check may run.
Returns:

0, SIGNAL_EXIT after SIGTERM or SIGINT, or HOST_CHECK_EXIT.

Runner = typing.Callable[[typing.Sequence[str]], str]

Runs a command (sbatch, squeue, scancel) and returns its stdout.

STALE_REASONS = ('Priority', 'QOS', 'ReqNodeNotAvail')

Pending reasons (prefixes) that make a partition stale after pending_s; Resources is not one.

HELD_REASONS = ('JobHeld', 'launch failed requeued held')

Pending reasons (prefixes) of held jobs, which never start on their own: stale at once.

LIVE_STATES = ('PENDING', 'RUNNING', 'CONFIGURING', 'SUSPENDED', 'REQUEUED')

Worker job states that count as live.

SQUEUE_FORMAT = '%i|%P|%T|%V|%j|%r'

Job id, partition, state, submit time, name and reason; the reason last, as it may hold spaces.

1241class ResourceClass:
1242    """A resource class the caller defines, and the partitions that offer it (in order of preference on ties).

1255            raise ValueError(f"resource class {self.name!r} needs a plain name and at least one partition")

1257    @classmethod
1258    def from_dict(cls, data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> ResourceClass:
1259        """A class from ``{name, partitions: [{partition, cpus, mem, time, gres, exclude, requeue, max_workers}]}``."""
1260        parts = []
1261        for row in data["partitions"]:
1262            row = dict(row)
1263            if "exclude" in row:
1264                row["exclude"] = tuple(str(n) for n in row["exclude"] or ())
1265            parts.append(PartitionSpec(**row))
1266        return cls(name=str(data["name"]), partitions=tuple(parts))

class Controller: 
1306class Controller:
1307    """Keeps Slurm workers on every partition that offers a class, in step with the pool's queue."""
1308
1309    def __init__(
1310        self,
1311        pool: WorkPool,
1312        classes: Sequence[ResourceClass],
1313        *,
1314        runner: Runner = run_command,
1315        worker_command: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
1316        poll_s: float = 30.0,
1317        pending_s: float = 600.0,
1318        release_cap: int = 3,
1319        release_window_s: float = 3600.0,
1320        log_dir: Optional[PathLike] = None,
1321        clock: Callable[[], float] = time.time,
1322    ) -> None:
1323        """Set up a controller; nothing is submitted until :meth:`tick`.
1324
1325        Args:
1326            pool: The pool.
1327            classes: The resource classes and their partitions.
1328            runner: Runs ``sbatch``, ``squeue`` and ``scancel``.
1329            worker_command: The worker's argv up to ``--classes`` (default: this interpreter running
1330                ``python -m senselab.utils.work_pool work POOL``).
1331            poll_s: Seconds between ticks in :meth:`run`.
1332            pending_s: A partition whose workers have been pending this long for a stale reason gets none.
1333            release_cap: Host-check releases on a partition within ``release_window_s`` that pause it.
1334            release_window_s: The release cap's window.
1335            log_dir: Where workers write ``%x-%j.out`` (default: sbatch's default).
1336            clock: The local clock, against which squeue's submit times are aged.
1337        """
1338        self.pool, self.classes, self.runner = pool, list(classes), runner
1339        self.worker_command = list(worker_command or [sys.executable, "-m", "senselab.utils.work_pool", "work"])
1340        if worker_command is None:
1341            self.worker_command.append(str(pool.root))
1342        self.poll_s, self.pending_s = poll_s, pending_s
1343        self.release_cap, self.release_window_s = release_cap, release_window_s
1344        self.log_dir = Path(log_dir).absolute() if log_dir is not None else None
1345        self.clock = clock
1346        self.pool8 = pool_tag(pool)
1347
1348    def job_name(self, cls: str) -> str:
1349        """The job name of this pool's workers of class ``cls``."""
1350        return f"work-pool-{self.pool8}-{cls}"
1351
1352    def _jobs(self) -> list[_Job]:
1353        names = {self.job_name(c.name): c.name for c in self.classes}
1354        out = self.runner(["squeue", "--me", "-h", f"--name={','.join(names)}", "-o", SQUEUE_FORMAT])
1355        jobs = []
1356        for line in out.splitlines():
1357            fields = line.strip().split("|", 5)
1358            if len(fields) < 6 or fields[4] not in names:
1359                continue
1360            job_id, partition, state, submitted, name, reason = fields
1361            jobs.append(_Job(job_id, partition, state, _submit_time(submitted), names[name], reason))
1362        return jobs
1363
1364    def _render(self, cls: ResourceClass, spec: PartitionSpec) -> list[str]:
1365        argv = [
1366            "sbatch",
1367            "--parsable",
1368            f"--partition={spec.partition}",
1369            f"--job-name={self.job_name(cls.name)}",
1370            f"--cpus-per-task={spec.cpus}",
1371            f"--mem={spec.mem}",
1372            f"--time={spec.time}",
1373        ]
1374        if spec.gres:
1375            argv.append(f"--gres={spec.gres}")
1376        if spec.exclude:
1377            argv.append(f"--exclude={','.join(spec.exclude)}")
1378        if spec.requeue:
1379            argv.append("--requeue")
1380        if self.log_dir is not None:
1381            argv.append(f"--output={self.log_dir}/%x-%j.out")
1382        # exec: the worker replaces sbatch's wrapper shell, so a cancel or preemption SIGTERM reaches it and it can
1383        # release its item (a shell dying first ends the step, and Slurm then kills the worker outright).
1384        argv += ["--wrap", "exec " + shlex.join([*self.worker_command, "--classes", cls.name])]
1385        return argv
1386
1387    def _stale(self, job: _Job, now: float) -> bool:
1388        if job.state != "PENDING":
1389            return False
1390        if job.reason.startswith(HELD_REASONS):
1391            return True
1392        return (
1393            job.reason.startswith(STALE_REASONS) and job.submitted is not None and now - job.submitted > self.pending_s
1394        )
1395
1396    def _cdir(self, name: str) -> Path:
1397        path = self.pool.root / "controller" / name
1398        path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1399        return path
1400
1401    def _record_job(self, job_id: str, cls: str, partition: str) -> None:
1402        """Record a job this controller submitted (only recorded jobs are ever cancelled)."""
1403        _write_json(self._cdir("jobs") / f"{job_id}.json", {"job": job_id, "class": cls, "partition": partition})
1404
1405    def _recorded(self) -> set[str]:
1406        return {n[: -len(".json")] for n in _names(self._cdir("jobs")) if n.endswith(".json")}
1407
1408    def _cancel(self, ids: Sequence[str]) -> list[str]:
1409        """``scancel --state=PENDING`` the recorded ones of ``ids`` (a worker that started meanwhile is left alone)."""
1410        recorded = self._recorded()
1411        mine = [i for i in ids if i in recorded]
1412        if not mine:
1413            return []
1414        try:
1415            self.runner(["scancel", "--state=PENDING", *mine])
1416        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
1417            _log(f"control: scancel failed ({exc}); retrying next tick")
1418            return []
1419        return mine
1420
1421    def _marked_stale(self, partition: str, now: float) -> bool:
1422        """Whether this controller cancelled stale workers on ``partition`` within ``pending_s`` (storage clock)."""
1423        safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", partition)
1424        changed = _fresh_mtime(self._cdir("stale") / safe)
1425        return changed is not None and now - changed <= self.pending_s
1426
1427    def _mark_stale(self, partition: str) -> None:
1428        safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]", "_", partition)
1429        path = self._cdir("stale") / safe
1430        os.close(os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT, 0o660))
1431        os.utime(path)
1432
1433    def tick(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
1434        """Reap, count, then submit workers where items exceed live workers and cancel workers nobody needs.
1435
1436        Pending workers on a stale or paused partition do not count as live: they are cancelled (when this pool's
1437        controller submitted them) and the partition gets no workers for ``pending_s``, so the work goes elsewhere.
1438        A failed ``sbatch`` skips its partition for the rest of the tick.
1439
1440        Returns:
1441            ``{"reaped", "submitted": [{class, partition, job}], "cancelled": [job ids], "failed": [partitions],
1442            "partitions": {p: {pending, running, stale, host_check_releases, paused}}, "status"}``; the same
1443            ``partitions`` go into ``status.json``.
1444
1445        Raises:
1446            OSError: The pool could not be read or written.
1447            subprocess.SubprocessError: ``squeue`` failed.
1448        """
1449        reaped = self.pool.reap()
1450        status = self.pool.status()
1451        jobs = [j for j in self._jobs() if j.state in LIVE_STATES]
1452        now = self.clock()
1453        storage_now = self.pool._server_now()
1454        releases = self.pool.host_check_failures(self.release_window_s)
1455        partitions: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
1456        for p in dict.fromkeys(spec.partition for c in self.classes for spec in c.partitions):
1457            mine = [j for j in jobs if j.partition == p]
1458            partitions[p] = {
1459                "pending": sum(j.state == "PENDING" for j in mine),
1460                "running": sum(j.state != "PENDING" for j in mine),
1461                "stale": any(self._stale(j, now) for j in mine) or self._marked_stale(p, storage_now),
1462                "host_check_releases": releases.get(p, 0),
1463                "paused": "host-check" if releases.get(p, 0) >= self.release_cap else None,
1464            }
1465
1466        def blocked(p: str) -> bool:
1467            row = partitions.get(p)
1468            return row is not None and bool(row["stale"] or row["paused"])
1469
1470        submitted: list[dict[str, str]] = []
1471        cancelled: list[str] = []
1472        failed: list[str] = []
1473        for cls in self.classes:
1474            row = status["classes"].get(cls.name, {})
1475            queued, leased = int(row.get("queued", 0)), int(row.get("leased", 0))
1476            ours = [j for j in jobs if j.cls == cls.name]
1477            stuck = [j for j in ours if j.state == "PENDING" and blocked(j.partition)]
1478            live = [j for j in ours if j not in stuck]
1479            if queued == 0:
1480                cancelled += self._cancel([j.id for j in ours if j.state == "PENDING"])
1481                continue
1482            gone = self._cancel([j.id for j in stuck])
1483            cancelled += gone
1484            for p in dict.fromkeys(j.partition for j in stuck if j.id in gone):
1485                self._mark_stale(p)
1486            pending = {
1487                s.partition: [j for j in live if j.partition == s.partition and j.state == "PENDING"]
1488                for s in cls.partitions
1489            }
1490            count = {s.partition: sum(j.partition == s.partition for j in live) for s in cls.partitions}
1491            npend = {p: len(js) for p, js in pending.items()}
1492            oldest = {
1493                p: max((now - j.submitted for j in js if j.submitted is not None), default=0.0)
1494                for p, js in pending.items()
1495            }
1496            usable = [(k, s) for k, s in enumerate(cls.partitions) if not blocked(s.partition)]
1497            wanted = queued + leased - len(live)
1498            while wanted > 0:
1499                room = [(k, s) for k, s in usable if count[s.partition] < s.max_workers and s.partition not in failed]
1500                if not room:
1501                    break
1502                _, spec = min(room, key=lambda ks: (npend[ks[1].partition], oldest[ks[1].partition], ks[0]))
1503                try:
1504                    job_id = self.runner(self._render(cls, spec)).strip().split(";")[0]
1505                except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
1506                    _log(f"control: sbatch on {spec.partition} failed ({exc}); skipping it this tick")
1507                    failed.append(spec.partition)
1508                    continue
1509                self._record_job(job_id, cls.name, spec.partition)
1510                wanted -= 1
1511                submitted.append({"class": cls.name, "partition": spec.partition, "job": job_id})
1512                count[spec.partition] += 1
1513                npend[spec.partition] += 1
1514                partitions[spec.partition]["pending"] += 1
1515        _write_json(self.pool.root / "status.json", {**status, "partitions": partitions})
1516        return {
1517            "reaped": reaped,
1518            "submitted": submitted,
1519            "cancelled": cancelled,
1520            "failed": failed,
1521            "partitions": partitions,
1522            "status": status,
1523        }
1524
1525    def run(self, once: bool = False) -> int:
1526        """Hold the pool's controller lock and tick every ``poll_s`` until nothing is queued, leased or staged.
1527
1528        A tick that fails (a Slurm command, or the pool's storage) is logged and retried after ``poll_s``.
1529
1530        Args:
1531            once: Tick once and return.
1532
1533        Returns:
1534            0; 1 when ``once`` and the tick failed; :data:`CONTROLLER_LOCKED_EXIT` when another controller runs.
1535        """
1536        lock = open(self._cdir("") / "lock", "a")  # noqa: SIM115 — held for the whole run
1537        try:
1538            try:
1539                fcntl.lockf(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
1540            except OSError:
1541                _log(f"control: another controller holds {self.pool.root}/controller/lock; exiting")
1542                return CONTROLLER_LOCKED_EXIT
1543            while True:
1544                try:
1545                    summary = self.tick()
1546                except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
1547                    _log(f"control: tick failed ({exc!r}); retrying in {self.poll_s} s")
1548                    if once:
1549                        return 1
1550                    time.sleep(self.poll_s)
1551                    continue
1552                counts = summary["status"]["counts"]
1553                _log(
1554                    f"control: reaped {summary['reaped']}, submitted {len(summary['submitted'])}, cancelled "
1555                    f"{len(summary['cancelled'])}; queued {counts['queued']} leased {counts['leased']} done "
1556                    f"{counts['done']} dead {counts['dead']}"
1557                )
1558                if once or counts["queued"] + counts["leased"] + counts["staged"] == 0:
1559                    return 0
1560                time.sleep(self.poll_s)
1561        finally:
1562            lock.close()

Keeps Slurm workers on every partition that offers a class, in step with the pool's queue.

1323        """Set up a controller; nothing is submitted until :meth:`tick`.
1324
1325        Args:
1326            pool: The pool.
1327            classes: The resource classes and their partitions.
1328            runner: Runs ``sbatch``, ``squeue`` and ``scancel``.
1329            worker_command: The worker's argv up to ``--classes`` (default: this interpreter running
1330                ``python -m senselab.utils.work_pool work POOL``).
1331            poll_s: Seconds between ticks in :meth:`run`.
1332            pending_s: A partition whose workers have been pending this long for a stale reason gets none.
1333            release_cap: Host-check releases on a partition within ``release_window_s`` that pause it.
1334            release_window_s: The release cap's window.
1335            log_dir: Where workers write ``%x-%j.out`` (default: sbatch's default).
1336            clock: The local clock, against which squeue's submit times are aged.
1337        """
1338        self.pool, self.classes, self.runner = pool, list(classes), runner
1339        self.worker_command = list(worker_command or [sys.executable, "-m", "senselab.utils.work_pool", "work"])
1340        if worker_command is None:
1341            self.worker_command.append(str(pool.root))
1342        self.poll_s, self.pending_s = poll_s, pending_s
1343        self.release_cap, self.release_window_s = release_cap, release_window_s
1344        self.log_dir = Path(log_dir).absolute() if log_dir is not None else None
1345        self.clock = clock
1346        self.pool8 = pool_tag(pool)

def submit_controller( pool: WorkPool, classes_file: Union[str, pathlib.Path], *, partition: str, time: str, runner: Callable[[Sequence[str]], str] = <function run_command>, poll_s: float = 30.0, cpus: int = 1, mem: str = '2G', output: Union[str, pathlib.Path, NoneType] = None, extra_args: Sequence[str] = ()) -> str: 
1565def submit_controller(
1566    pool: WorkPool,
1567    classes_file: PathLike,
1568    *,
1569    partition: str,
1570    time: str,
1571    runner: Runner = run_command,
1572    poll_s: float = 30.0,
1573    cpus: int = 1,
1574    mem: str = "2G",
1575    output: Optional[PathLike] = None,
1576    extra_args: Sequence[str] = (),
1577) -> str:
1578    """Submit a small job that runs ``control POOL --classes FILE`` until the pool drains.
1579
1580    Args:
1581        pool: The pool.
1582        classes_file: The resource classes' YAML file.
1583        partition: The controller job's partition.
1584        time: Its ``--time``.
1585        runner: Runs ``sbatch``.
1586        poll_s: Seconds between ticks.
1587        cpus: Its ``--cpus-per-task``.
1588        mem: Its ``--mem``.
1589        output: Its ``--output``, when set.
1590        extra_args: More ``control`` arguments (e.g. ``--host-check``).
1591
1592    Returns:
1593        The controller's job id.
1594    """
1595    command = [sys.executable, "-m", "senselab.utils.work_pool", "control", str(pool.root)]
1596    command += ["--classes", str(Path(classes_file).absolute()), "--poll", str(float(poll_s)), *extra_args]
1597    argv = [
1598        "sbatch",
1599        "--parsable",
1600        f"--partition={partition}",
1601        f"--job-name=work-pool-control-{pool_tag(pool)}",
1602        f"--cpus-per-task={cpus}",
1603        f"--mem={mem}",
1604        f"--time={time}",
1605    ]
1606    if output is not None:
1607        argv.append(f"--output={output}")
1608    argv += ["--wrap", "exec " + shlex.join(command)]
1609    return runner(argv).strip().split(";")[0]

def main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int: 
1612def main(argv: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> int:
1613    """Command line: ``work`` runs one worker, ``control`` runs a controller.
1614
1615    ``work POOL --classes a,b [--linger N] [--poll S] [--worker NAME] [--host-check CMD] [--host-check-timeout S]``;
1616    ``control POOL --classes FILE [--once] [--poll S] [--pending-s S] [--release-cap N] [--log-dir D]
1617    [--host-check CMD] [--host-check-timeout S] [--worker-linger N] [--worker-poll S]``.
1618
1619    Args:
1620        argv: Arguments (default ``sys.argv[1:]``).
1621
1622    Returns:
1623        The exit code.
1624    """
1625    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m senselab.utils.work_pool")
1626    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
1627    run = sub.add_parser("work", help="run one worker")
1628    run.add_argument("pool")
1629    run.add_argument("--classes", required=True, help="comma-separated resource classes")
1630    run.add_argument("--linger", type=int, default=3)
1631    run.add_argument("--poll", type=float, default=10.0)
1632    run.add_argument("--worker")
1633    run.add_argument("--host-check", help="a command (split like a shell) that must succeed on this node")
1634    run.add_argument("--host-check-timeout", type=float, default=HOST_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S)
1635    ctl = sub.add_parser("control", help="run a controller that submits and cancels Slurm workers")
1636    ctl.add_argument("pool")
1637    ctl.add_argument("--classes", required=True, help="the resource classes' YAML file")
1638    ctl.add_argument("--once", action="store_true", help="tick once and exit")
1639    ctl.add_argument("--poll", type=float, default=30.0)
1640    ctl.add_argument("--pending-s", type=float, default=600.0)
1641    ctl.add_argument("--release-cap", type=int, default=3)
1642    ctl.add_argument("--log-dir")
1643    ctl.add_argument("--host-check", help="passed on to each worker")
1644    ctl.add_argument("--host-check-timeout", type=float, help="passed on to each worker")
1645    ctl.add_argument("--worker-linger", type=int, help="passed on to each worker as --linger")
1646    ctl.add_argument("--worker-poll", type=float, help="passed on to each worker as --poll")
1647    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
1648    if args.cmd == "control":
1649        pool = WorkPool(args.pool)
1650        command = [sys.executable, "-m", "senselab.utils.work_pool", "work", str(pool.root)]
1651        if args.host_check:
1652            command += ["--host-check", args.host_check]
1653        if args.host_check_timeout is not None:
1654            command += ["--host-check-timeout", str(args.host_check_timeout)]
1655        if args.worker_linger is not None:
1656            command += ["--linger", str(args.worker_linger)]
1657        if args.worker_poll is not None:
1658            command += ["--poll", str(args.worker_poll)]
1659        controller = Controller(
1660            pool,
1661            load_classes(args.classes),
1662            worker_command=command,
1663            poll_s=args.poll,
1664            pending_s=args.pending_s,
1665            release_cap=args.release_cap,
1666            log_dir=args.log_dir,
1667        )
1668        return controller.run(once=args.once)
1669    classes = [c for c in args.classes.split(",") if c]
1670    check = shlex.split(args.host_check) if args.host_check else None
1671    return work(
1672        args.pool,
1673        classes,
1674        worker=args.worker,
1675        linger=args.linger,
1676        poll_s=args.poll,
1677        host_check=check,
1678        host_check_timeout_s=args.host_check_timeout,
1679    )

Command line: work runs one worker, control runs a controller.

work POOL --classes a,b [--linger N] [--poll S] [--worker NAME] [--host-check CMD] [--host-check-timeout S]; control POOL --classes FILE [--once] [--poll S] [--pending-s S] [--release-cap N] [--log-dir D] [--host-check CMD] [--host-check-timeout S] [--worker-linger N] [--worker-poll S].

Arguments:
  • argv: Arguments (default sys.argv[1:]).
Returns:

The exit code.
